children: BTCUSD climbed ~12% over seven days to $87,315 Monday, its highest since late January. Bitcoin spot ETFs saw about $1B inflows Monday and $1.5B+ since mid-last week.
BTCUSD hit resistance near $90,000; short-term sellers active $86k–$88k. Additional resistance $88k–$90k at the 100-week MA. A sustained close above those levels matters to bulls.
BTCUSD perpetual open interest rose to about $160B, the highest since late October, while over $920M of short positions were liquidated during the recent rally.
BTCUSD closed Sept 20 at $81,159, trading above its 50-week moving average ($78,786) for the first time in 45 weeks amid recent volatility.
Spot ETF flows shifted from early-week outflows to late-week inflows, trimming weekly net outflows to about $6M and accompanying a BTCUSD spot CFD price rebound.
Fidelity International’s global macro director said BTCUSD Spot needs to hold above ~$85,500 to enter a new bull phase, citing that level as a key market-sentiment threshold.
BTCUSD MVRV rose above its 365‑day moving average, climbing from ~1.19 on Aug 16 to ~1.62 in the latest reading, signaling higher market value vs realized value over the past year.
CryptoQuant says BTCUSD 30-day MVRV moving average above 1.5 may end bear-market accumulation; a rise past 1.62 could push spot BTCUSD toward prior highs near $126,200.
BTCUSD traded above its 365‑day moving average as gains outpaced the long‑term trend; on‑chain shows limited profit‑taking. Softer oil and higher US Treasury buybacks supported risk appetite.
Large holders and exchanges moved in tandem in BTCUSD; flows into U.S. spot ETFs and Fed policy linked. Traders watch $80,500 support and potential breakout toward $88,000–$90,000.
